calls.video_title: He Called the 1987 Crash. Now He’s Calling This
calls.thesis: BUY, first tracked XLK call for MarketBeat (guest Dr Mark Skousen, Oxford Club; no flip) — 'I recommend XLK, which is the technology fund': his preferred way to own new technology is a broad-based ETF or mutual fund because picking individual winners is luck. He says XLK has outperformed QQQ by about 30% (per year, as captioned) and has kept up with the S&P 500 this year.
calls.base_case: XLK holds Apple, Microsoft, Broadcom and Palantir (captions garble it as 'Palunteer') — mainly software and established tech; it does not hold Tesla or SpaceX, which he sees as high-risk, high-potential.
calls.bull_case: Broad diversification removes single-stock risk in a sector where winners are hard to pick in advance, while tech/AI remains, in his words, a golden age of investing technology and the main driver of the market.
calls.bear_case: Tech multiples are high and he is cautious overall: rising rates, stubborn inflation and high AI multiples mean investors 'have to be very careful' even in the one area still working.
